newsitem.title: USA: Steelworkers reach tentative pact with Bridgestone.
newsitem.headline: Steelworkers reach tentative pact with Bridgestone.

text.p: The United Steelworkers union and Bridgestone/Firestone Inc. said Tuesday they reached a tentative agreement in their long and bitter labour dispute.
Spokesmen for the company and the union declined to give details of the agreement, but union spokesman Howard Scott said the contract was tentative and under review by local union presidents.

Bridgestone/Firestone, based in Nashville, Tenn., is the U.S. arm of Japanese tiremaker Bridgestone Corp. The union planned a news conference on Wednesday in Pittsburgh to discuss details of the agreement.
About 5,500 workers are covered by the tentative pact. Union members will hold a ratification vote to approve pact, but no date has been set.
Union members struck the tire maker in July 1994. At that time, workers were represented by the former United Rubber Workers union.

The company hired replacement workers in January 1995. The following July, the rubber workers merged with the steelworkers and launched a "corporate campaign" against the company that targeted car dealers, tire distributors and consumers, seeking a boycott of Bridgestone/Firestone products.
The strike affected five U.S. tire plants mostly in the Midwest, and prompted Labour Secretary Robert Reich to request several meetings with Bridgestone. The company refused the requests.
In May 1995, the union then offered an unconditional return to work, thereby ending the strike.

Workers were recalled periodically for several months, and by September of this year virtually all workers had been called back. However, union members were working under contract proposals offered by the company before the strike began.
